meta.spec_reference: PNG (Portable Network Graphics) Specification, Version 1.2 (W3C/PNG Development Group, 1999-07-14, http://www.libpng.org/pub/png/spec/1.2/); ISO/IEC 15948:2004 for chunk-ordering restatements; APNG (Animated PNG) Specification 1.0 (https://wiki.mozilla.org/APNG_Specification) for acTL/fcTL/fdAT; RFC 1950 (zlib) and RFC 1951 (DEFLATE) for compressed datastreams; CRC-32/ISO-HDLC (ITU-T V.42) for the per-chunk CRC

schema_extensions.name: comparison_sites
schema_extensions.why: This template contains no ReadUByte/ReadUShort/ReadByte/ReadBytes lookahead calls at all, so the `lookahead` key never applies. The equivalent 'good known values' that FormatFuzzer would mine are the sixteen literal string comparisons `type.cname == "XXXX"` in the dispatch chain (lines 301-330) plus the two ordering checks at lines 382 and 385. comparison_sites records each of those call sites with its line, verbatim snippet and compared literal so the rewrite step gets a per-call-site value set rather than only a merged global set.

schema_extensions.name: unused_in_parse_flow
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries for PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA.profile_name and PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA.red
schema_extensions.why: PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA is typedef'd at lines 95-98 but is never instantiated: the chunk dispatch chain (lines 301-331) has no `iCCP` branch, so iCCP chunks fall through to the generic `ubyte data[length]` path. The flag tells the rewrite step that these entries describe a declared-but-dead type, so it may either wire up an iCCP branch using them or skip them, but must not assume the struct is currently reachable.

schema_extensions.name: bit_semantics
schema_extensions.why: PNG encodes four independent property flags in bit 5 (0x20) of the four chunk-type bytes. readCHUNK (lines 354-357) tests each one explicitly. A per-byte bitmask_constraint is the only way to record that bit 5 of byte 2 MUST be zero (reserved) while the other three bits are free, which no whole-field constraint on cname can express.

schema_extensions.name: template_deviations
schema_extensions.why: The .bt disagrees with the PNG specification in several places (signed int16 used for unsigned 16-bit spec fields, an inner struct reading the enclosing chunk's `length` variable by scope capture, a mis-named field, a dead typedef, and length arithmetic that underflows on malformed input). A generator that faithfully reproduced the template's declared types would emit spec-invalid files, so these must be visible as data, not buried in prose.

schema_extensions.name: byte_layout
schema_extensions.where: optional key on constraints entries whose byte size or element size is not obvious from field_type
schema_extensions.why: Several array fields (PLTE entries, sPLT entries, fdAT payload) have an element size the .bt does not state directly; the rewrite step needs it to emit a self-consistent length field.

schema_extensions.name: evidence.line and evidence.snippet retained on spec-sourced entries
schema_extensions.where: the 26 constraints entries whose source is "spec" but whose field is nonetheless declared in the .bt
schema_extensions.why: The schema pairs source "spec" with an evidence object holding only a note. For a field that the template declares but never checks (tIME's month, fcTL's offsets, IHDR's width) the rule genuinely comes from the specification, yet the field has a real declaration line the rewrite step needs in order to place it. These entries carry the required note plus the declaration site, so nothing specified is dropped and the anchor is not lost.

meta.structure_note: A fixed 8-byte signature followed by a stream of self-describing chunks, each laid out as [uint32 length][char[4] type][length payload bytes][uint32 CRC-32 over type+payload]; the stream must begin with IHDR, contain at least one IDAT, and terminate with a zero-length IEND.

PNG_SIGNATURE.btPngSignature[0].description: First 16-bit word of the 8-byte PNG file signature: the high-bit byte 0x89 that defeats 7-bit-clean transfers, followed by ASCII 'P'.

PNG_SIGNATURE.btPngSignature[1].description: Second 16-bit word of the PNG signature: ASCII 'N' 'G', completing the '\x89PNG' magic.

PNG_SIGNATURE.btPngSignature[2].description: Third 16-bit word of the PNG signature: CR LF, the DOS line ending used to detect CRLF-to-LF text-mode mangling.

PNG_SIGNATURE.btPngSignature[3].description: Fourth 16-bit word of the PNG signature: DOS end-of-file (0x1A) followed by LF, which stops MS-DOS TYPE and detects LF-to-CRLF mangling.

PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA.profile_name.description: NUL-terminated ICC colour-profile name; a PNG keyword of 1-79 Latin-1 printable characters with no leading, trailing or consecutive spaces.
PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA.profile_name.pattern: ^[\x20-\x7E\xA1-\xFF](?:[\x20-\x7E\xA1-\xFF]{0,77}[\x20-\x7E\xA1-\xFF])?\x00$ with no leading space, no trailing space and no two consecutive spaces; total length 1-79 characters before the terminating NUL

generation_range.rationale: Keyword length in characters. The spec allows 79 but short ASCII keywords keep the chunk small and exercise the same code paths.

PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA.profile_name.notes: PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA is declared but never instantiated: the dispatch chain at lines 301-331 has no iCCP branch, so real iCCP chunks are consumed by the generic `ubyte data[length]` path at line 332.

PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA.red.description: Mis-named field: at this byte offset the iCCP chunk carries the compression method for the embedded ICC profile, and PNG defines only method 0 (zlib/deflate).

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.3 (iCCP Embedded ICC profile): the byte following the NUL-terminated profile name is the compression method, and the only value defined is 0 (deflate/inflate with zlib wrapper). The template names it `red`, which is wrong for iCCP; the declared field is a single ubyte at the correct offset, so the spec rule attaches to it.

CTYPE.cname.description: Four-byte chunk type code; the template dispatches on its exact ASCII spelling, and every registered PNG 1.2 / APNG 1.0 chunk type is drawn from [A-Za-z]{4}.
CTYPE.cname.notes: The template header comment at lines 29-30 notes that PNG only *encourages* [a-zA-Z]{4}; in practice every decoder treats a non-alphabetic type byte as a corrupt stream. IDAT, gAMA, iCCP, hIST and tRNS are handled by the generic `ubyte data[length]` path at line 332 rather than a dedicated branch, but are still legal and in IDAT's case mandatory. This template contains no ReadUByte/ReadUShort/ReadBytes lookahead calls, so `lookahead` is not applicable anywhere in this file; see comparison_sites instead.

CTYPE.cname[0].description: First chunk-type byte; bit 5 (0x20, i.e. lowercase) is the ancillary flag: clear means the chunk is critical and a decoder must abort if it does not understand it, set means ancillary.
CTYPE.cname[0].valid_bits: 0x20 is the ancillary property bit; the remaining bits must still form an ASCII letter, so the byte itself lies in 0x41-0x5A (critical) or 0x61-0x7A (ancillary)
CTYPE.cname[0].notes: valid_values lists the two legal states of the masked bit, not of the whole byte.

CTYPE.cname[1].description: Second chunk-type byte; bit 5 (0x20) is the private flag: clear means a public, registered chunk type, set means a private/application-specific type.
CTYPE.cname[1].valid_bits: 0x20 is the private property bit; the byte must remain an ASCII letter, 0x41-0x5A (public) or 0x61-0x7A (private)

CTYPE.cname[2].description: Third chunk-type byte; bit 5 (0x20) is reserved and MUST be 0, so this byte must be an uppercase ASCII letter in every conforming PNG file.
CTYPE.cname[2].valid_bits: 0x20 is the reserved property bit and must be clear; the byte must be an uppercase ASCII letter, 0x41-0x5A
CTYPE.cname[2].notes: The template flags a set reserved bit as ERROR_RESERVED in the chunk label but does not refuse to parse; the specification makes it a hard requirement. Every chunk type in CTYPE.cname's valid_values already satisfies it.

CTYPE.cname[3].description: Fourth chunk-type byte; bit 5 (0x20) is the safe-to-copy flag: clear means an editor that does not understand the chunk must not copy it past a critical-chunk change, set means it may.
CTYPE.cname[3].valid_bits: 0x20 is the safe-to-copy property bit; the byte must remain an ASCII letter, 0x41-0x5A (unsafe to copy) or 0x61-0x7A (safe to copy)

CTYPE.ctype.description: The same four chunk-type bytes viewed as one big-endian uint32; it is a union alias of cname, so it must carry the numeric encoding of one of the legal four-character type codes.
CTYPE.ctype.notes: Union member overlapping CTYPE.cname at lines 112-115: writing either one writes the same four bytes. A generator must emit these four bytes exactly once, not twice.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.width.description: Image width in pixels; zero is explicitly illegal and the value is limited to a PNG four-byte unsigned integer.

generation_range.rationale: Decoders allocate width*height*channels bytes on sight of IHDR. Spec-legal widths up to 2^31-1 make a single generated file trigger multi-gigabyte allocations and dominate fuzzing runtime; 1-64 keeps every produced image trivially small while still exercising all width-dependent code (row stride, filtering, Adam7 pass geometry).

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.1.1 (IHDR): 'Width and height give the image dimensions in pixels. They are 4-byte integers. Zero is an invalid value.' Like all PNG four-byte unsigned integers the value must not exceed 2^31-1 (section 3.2). The template declares a plain uint32 and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.height.description: Image height in pixels; zero is explicitly illegal and the value is limited to a PNG four-byte unsigned integer.

generation_range.rationale: Same allocation blow-up as width; the product width*height is what a decoder reserves, so both must be capped together.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.1.1 (IHDR): 'Width and height give the image dimensions in pixels. They are 4-byte integers. Zero is an invalid value.' Bounded above by 2^31-1 per section 3.2. The template declares a plain uint32 and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.bits.description: Bit depth: number of bits per sample (per palette index for colour type 3); only five values exist and the legal subset narrows further with colour type.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.1.1 (IHDR): 'Bit depth is a single-byte integer giving the number of bits per sample or per palette index (not per pixel). Valid values are 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16, although not all values are allowed for all colour types.' The template declares it as a bare ubyte and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.bits.notes: Bit depth 8 is preferred: it is the only depth legal for every colour type, and it is the depth real decoders exercise most deeply.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.color_type.description: Colour type, a sum of the flags 1 (palette used), 2 (colour used) and 4 (alpha channel used); only five combinations are defined.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.color_type.notes: The whole enum body is lines 53-59. Colour types 1, 5 and 7 are deliberately absent. This field is read back by other chunks via chunk[0].ihdr.color_type at lines 320 and 322, so it drives the layout of bKGD and sBIT as well as its own validity.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.compr_method.description: Compression method for the IDAT image datastream; PNG 1.2 defines exactly one method, 0 (deflate with a 32K sliding window, zlib-wrapped).
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.compr_method.notes: Enum declared at lines 62-64 with the single member Deflate = 0; decoders are required to reject any other value.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.filter_method.description: Filter method (the preprocessing scheme applied to each scanline before compression); PNG 1.2 defines exactly one, 0 (adaptive filtering with five basic filter types).
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.filter_method.notes: Enum declared at lines 67-69 with the single member AdaptiveFiltering = 0.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.interlace_method.description: Interlace method: 0 for no interlacing (scanlines in order), 1 for the Adam7 seven-pass interlace.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.interlace_method.notes: Enum declared at lines 72-75. Method 0 is preferred: Adam7 changes the expected IDAT byte count in a way an uncompressed-payload generator cannot easily satisfy, so a mismatched interlace flag makes decoders bail before deep parsing.

PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.label.description: NUL-terminated tEXt keyword naming the text field; a PNG keyword of 1-79 printable Latin-1 characters with no leading, trailing or consecutive spaces.
PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.label.pattern: ^[\x20-\x7E\xA1-\xFF]{1,79}\x00$ with no leading space, no trailing space and no two consecutive spaces

generation_range.rationale: Keyword length in characters; short registered keywords keep the chunk small and are what real decoders special-case.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.3.1 (tEXt): 'The keyword must be at least one character and less than 80 characters long. Keywords are always interpreted according to the ISO 8859-1 (Latin-1) character set. They must contain only printable Latin-1 characters and spaces; that is, only character codes 32-126 and 161-255 decimal are allowed. To reduce the chances for human misreading of a keyword, leading and trailing spaces are forbidden, as are consecutive spaces.' The template reads it as an unchecked NUL-terminated string.

PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.data.description: The tEXt value string; its byte count is not stored anywhere but is derived from the enclosing chunk length minus the keyword and its NUL terminator, so the two must agree exactly.
PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.data.covers: the tEXt value bytes that follow the NUL terminator of `label`, to the end of the chunk payload; it excludes the enclosing chunk's length, type and CRC fields, and excludes `label` and its NUL

generation_range.rationale: Value-string byte count. tEXt payloads are unbounded in the spec (up to the 2^31-1 chunk limit); capping at 64 bytes keeps text chunks from dominating file size.

evidence.snippet: char   data[length - Strlen(label) - 1];   // rest of the data

PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.data.notes: `length` here is the enclosing PNG_CHUNK.length captured by 010 Editor's lexical scoping, not a member of PNG_CHUNK_TEXT. The value is *not* NUL-terminated and must not contain a NUL byte. If Strlen(label)+1 exceeds length the expression goes negative, which is the template's main malformed-input failure mode for tEXt.

PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData.description: Palette entry array; the number of entries is not stored but is the chunk length divided by three, so the chunk length must be an exact multiple of 3 and must not describe more than 256 entries.
PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData.algorithm: entry count = PNG_CHUNK.length / 3, with PNG_CHUNK.length required to be an exact multiple of 3 and in the range 3..768
PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData.covers: the entire PLTE chunk payload; each entry is exactly three bytes (red, green, blue), and the array excludes the enclosing chunk's length, type and CRC fields
PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData.byte_layout: 3 bytes per entry: PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btRed, .btGreen, .btBlue, each an 8-bit sample regardless of IHDR bit depth

generation_range.rationale: Entry count. 256 is also the hard spec maximum, and for colour type 3 the count must not exceed 2^bit_depth, so a generator should pick min(256, 2^bits).

PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData.notes: PNG 1.2 section 4.1.2: 'The number of entries is determined from the chunk length. A chunk length not divisible by 3 is an error.' The individual R/G/B samples are free-form colour data and are deliberately not given their own constraints entries.

PNG_POINT.x.description: CIE 1931 x chromaticity coordinate of a cHRM white point or primary, stored as the true value multiplied by 100000 and rounded.

generation_range.rationale: Chromaticity coordinates are fixed-point values scaled by 100000 and in practice lie in 0.0-1.0, i.e. 0-100000. Real values are around 31270 (white x) or 64000 (red x). Values above 100000 are meaningless and colour-managed decoders reject or ignore them.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.2.1 (cHRM): 'Each value is encoded as a 4-byte unsigned integer, representing the x or y value times 100000.' PNG four-byte unsigned integers are capped at 2^31-1 (section 3.2). The template declares a plain uint32 and performs no check.

PNG_POINT.x.notes: Used four times inside PNG_CHUNK_CHRM (white, red, green, blue at lines 157-160).

PNG_POINT.y.description: CIE 1931 y chromaticity coordinate of a cHRM white point or primary, stored as the true value multiplied by 100000 and rounded.

generation_range.rationale: Same fixed-point 100000 scaling as PNG_POINT.x; sane sRGB values are around 32900 (white y) or 33000 (red y).

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.2.1 (cHRM): 'Each value is encoded as a 4-byte unsigned integer, representing the x or y value times 100000.' Capped at 2^31-1 per section 3.2. The template declares a plain uint32 and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_SRGB.srgbChunkData.description: sRGB rendering intent; the four ICC rendering intents are the only defined values and the chunk is exactly one byte long.
PNG_CHUNK_SRGB.srgbChunkData.notes: Enum declared at lines 88-93. PNG 1.2 section 4.2.2.4 lists exactly these four intents; a value of 4 or above is a spec violation even though the template accepts any byte.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtIdChunkData.description: NUL-terminated iTXt keyword; a PNG keyword of 1-79 printable Latin-1 characters with no leading, trailing or consecutive spaces.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtIdChunkData.pattern: ^[\x20-\x7E\xA1-\xFF]{1,79}\x00$ with no leading space, no trailing space and no two consecutive spaces

generation_range.rationale: Keyword length in characters; keeps the chunk small.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.3.3 (iTXt): the keyword field obeys the same 1-79 printable-Latin-1 rules as tEXt. The template reads it as an unchecked NUL-terminated string at line 168.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtCompressionFlag.description: iTXt compression flag: 0 means the text is stored uncompressed, 1 means it is a zlib datastream compressed with the method in the following byte.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.3.3 (iTXt): 'A compression flag of 0 means uncompressed text, 1 means compressed text.' No other value is defined; the template declares a plain byte and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtCompressionFlag.notes: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.3.3: 'A compression flag of 0 means uncompressed text, 1 means compressed text.' Flag 0 is strongly preferred for generation because it removes the requirement to emit a valid zlib stream, letting a decoder read the text and continue rather than aborting on an inflate error.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtComprMethod.description: iTXt compression method; PNG defines only method 0 (zlib deflate), and the byte must still be present and zero even when the compression flag is 0.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtComprMethod.notes: The enum pngCompressionMethod (lines 62-64) has the single member Deflate = 0. Section 4.2.3.3 requires the field to be present unconditionally and to be 0 when the compression flag is 1; when the flag is 0 the value is ignored by decoders but is conventionally 0.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtLanguageTag.description: NUL-terminated RFC-1766/3066 language tag identifying the language of the translated keyword and text; may be the empty string when unspecified.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.3.3 (iTXt): the language tag is a null-terminated ISO-646 (ASCII) string following RFC 1766, consisting of hyphen-separated words of 1 to 8 alphanumeric characters each; it may be the empty string. The template reads it as an unchecked NUL-terminated string.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtLanguageTag.notes: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.3.3: 'The language tag ... is a null-terminated string ... Language tags are ASCII, and consist of hyphen-separated words of 1-8 alphanumeric characters each.'

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtTranslatedKeyword.description: NUL-terminated UTF-8 translation of the keyword into the declared language; may be empty, and must contain no NUL byte other than its terminator.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtTranslatedKeyword.pattern: well-formed UTF-8 with no embedded NUL, terminated by a single \x00; may be zero characters long. Newline characters are forbidden.

generation_range.rationale: Character count; unbounded in the spec, kept short so iTXt chunks stay small.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.3.3 (iTXt): the translated keyword is a null-terminated UTF-8 string that may be empty, must contain no NUL other than its terminator, and must not contain newline characters. The template reads it as an unchecked NUL-terminated string.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtValChunkData.description: The iTXt text payload; its byte count is not stored and must be derived from the chunk length minus the four preceding variable and fixed fields, so all five must agree exactly.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtValChunkData.algorithm: byte count = PNG_CHUNK.length - Strlen(itxtIdChunkData) - 1 - Strlen(itxtLanguageTag) - 1 - Strlen(itxtTranslatedKeyword) - 1 - 2
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtValChunkData.covers: the text bytes from the end of the translated keyword's NUL to the end of the chunk payload; the three subtracted 1s are the three NUL terminators and the subtracted 2 is itxtCompressionFlag plus itxtComprMethod. It excludes the enclosing chunk's length, type and CRC fields.

generation_range.rationale: Text byte count; unbounded in the spec up to the chunk-length limit, capped so iTXt chunks do not dominate file size.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtValChunkData.notes: The array-size expression spans lines 173-177. When itxtCompressionFlag is 1 these bytes must be a valid zlib datastream (RFC 1950) whose inflated content is UTF-8; when it is 0 they are raw UTF-8 with no terminator.

PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtIdChunkData.description: NUL-terminated zTXt keyword; a PNG keyword of 1-79 printable Latin-1 characters with no leading, trailing or consecutive spaces.
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtIdChunkData.pattern: ^[\x20-\x7E\xA1-\xFF]{1,79}\x00$ with no leading space, no trailing space and no two consecutive spaces

generation_range.rationale: Keyword length in characters.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.3.2 (zTXt): the keyword field obeys the same 1-79 printable-Latin-1 rules as tEXt. The template reads it as an unchecked NUL-terminated string at line 181.

PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.comprMethod.description: zTXt compression method; PNG defines only method 0 (zlib deflate), and any other value makes the chunk undecodable.
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.comprMethod.notes: Enum pngCompressionMethod, lines 62-64, single member Deflate = 0.

PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.description: The compressed zTXt text; its byte count is derived from the chunk length minus the keyword, its NUL and the compression-method byte, and the bytes themselves must form a valid zlib datastream.
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.algorithm: byte count = PNG_CHUNK.length - Strlen(ztxtIdChunkData) - 2; the content itself is a zlib (RFC 1950) datastream wrapping a DEFLATE (RFC 1951) stream, terminated by an Adler-32 checksum of the uncompressed data
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.covers: the compressed text bytes from just after comprMethod to the end of the chunk payload; the subtracted 2 is the keyword's NUL terminator plus the one-byte comprMethod. It excludes the enclosing chunk's length, type and CRC fields.

generation_range.rationale: Compressed byte count. The minimum is the size of a zlib stream wrapping a single stored (BTYPE=00) DEFLATE block with an empty payload: 2 header bytes + 5 block bytes + 4 Adler-32 bytes = 11. Capped at 96 so zTXt chunks stay small.

PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.notes: The most productive generation strategy is a stored (uncompressed) DEFLATE block: bytes 78 01, then 01, LEN low, LEN high, ~LEN low, ~LEN high, then LEN literal bytes, then the big-endian Adler-32 of those bytes. That reaches the decoder's text handling instead of aborting in inflate. The Adler-32 inside this payload is a nested checksum the outer chunk CRC does not cover.

PNG_CHUNK_TIME.timeYear.description: Complete four-digit year of last image modification (not an offset from 1900); the spec declares it as a two-byte unsigned integer.

generation_range.rationale: Plausible modification years for a PNG file; keeps the value in the range date-formatting code in viewers can render without overflow, while still being a real 16-bit value.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.5 (tIME): 'Year: 2 bytes (complete; for example, 1995, not 95)'. The field is an unsigned 2-byte integer; the template declares int16 (signed) and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_TIME.timeYear.notes: Template deviation: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.5 specifies an unsigned 2-byte integer, but the template declares int16 (signed), so years above 32767 display negative. See meta template_deviations.

PNG_CHUNK_TIME.timeMonth.description: Month of last modification, 1-12; zero and values above 12 are invalid.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.5 (tIME): 'Month: 1 byte (1-12)'. The template declares a plain byte and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_TIME.timeDay.description: Day of month of last modification, 1-31.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.5 (tIME): 'Day: 1 byte (1-31)'. The spec does not require the day to be valid for the given month. The template declares a plain byte and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_TIME.timeDay.notes: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.5: 'Day: 1 byte (1-31)'. The spec does not require the day to be valid for the given month.

PNG_CHUNK_TIME.timeHour.description: Hour of last modification in 24-hour UTC, 0-23.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.5 (tIME): 'Hour: 1 byte (0-23)'. The template declares a plain byte and performs no check.
PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.5 (tIME): 'Minute: 1 byte (0-59)'. The template declares a plain byte and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_TIME.timeSec.description: Second of last modification, 0-60; 60 is allowed to represent a leap second.

evidence.note: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.5 (tIME): 'Second: 1 byte (0-60) (to allow for leap seconds)'. The template declares a plain byte and performs no check.

PNG_CHUNK_TIME.timeSec.notes: PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.5: 'Second: 1 byte (0-60) (to allow for leap seconds)'.

PNG_CHUNK_BKGD.bgColorPaletteIndex.description: Background colour as a palette index; present only for colour type 3, and must address an entry that actually exists in PLTE.

generation_range.rationale: The palette may legally contain as few as one entry, and the index must be strictly less than the PLTE entry count. Index 0 is the only value valid for every palette size, so a generator that does not track the palette length must emit 0.

PNG_CHUNK_BKGD.bgColorPaletteIndex.notes: Selected by `case 3:` of the switch at line 196, driven by chunk[0].ihdr.color_type passed in at line 320.

PNG_CHUNK_BKGD.bgGrayscalePixelValue.description: Background colour as a single greyscale sample; present only for colour types 0 and 4, and must be less than 2^bit_depth.

generation_range.rationale: The sample is always stored in two bytes but the high-order bits must be zero for any bit depth below 16. Capping at 255 keeps the value legal for every bit depth from 8 upward and harmless below that.

PNG_CHUNK_BKGD.bgGrayscalePixelValue.notes: Selected by `case 0:`/`case 4:` of the switch at line 196. PNG 1.2 section 4.2.4.1: the value is stored as two bytes regardless of bit depth, but 'if the image bit depth is less than 16, the least significant bits are used and the others are 0'.

PNG_CHUNK_BKGD.bgColorPixelRed.description: Red component of the background colour; present only for colour types 2 and 6, and must be less than 2^bit_depth.

generation_range.rationale: Two-byte storage but only the low bit_depth bits may be non-zero; 0-255 is safe for bit depth 8 and 16.

PNG_CHUNK_BKGD.bgColorPixelGreen.description: Green component of the background colour; present only for colour types 2 and 6, and must be less than 2^bit_depth.

generation_range.rationale: Two-byte storage but only the low bit_depth bits may be non-zero.

PNG_CHUNK_BKGD.bgColorPixelBlue.description: Blue component of the background colour; present only for colour types 2 and 6, and must be less than 2^bit_depth.

structure.subject: PNG_SIGNATURE
structure.detail: the 8-byte signature 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A occupies file offsets 0-7, before any chunk
structure.description: Every PNG datastream begins with the same fixed 8-byte signature and nothing may precede it.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed 8-byte head element with no randomisation and no evil-bit substitution

structure.subject: chunk type "IHDR"
structure.detail: must be the first chunk, i.e. chunk[0], immediately after the signature
structure.description: The image header must come first because every later chunk's meaning depends on its colour type and bit depth.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed head chunk before the bounded repeated middle section; the template's bKGD and sBIT branches read chunk[0].ihdr directly, so this position is load-bearing, not cosmetic

structure.subject: chunk type "IEND"
structure.detail: must be the final chunk, and its length must be 0 so the whole chunk is the 12 bytes 00 00 00 00 49 45 4E 44 AE 42 60 82
structure.description: The image trailer marks the end of the datastream and nothing may follow it.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed 12-byte tail element after the repeated middle section; the whole chunk including its CRC is a constant, so it can be written literally

structure.subject: chunk type "IDAT"
structure.detail: at least one IDAT chunk must be present
structure.description: A PNG datastream without image data is invalid however well formed its other chunks are.
structure.generation_bound: 1 to 3 IDAT chunks; each chunk payload capped at 4096 bytes, so the compressed stream never exceeds ~12 KiB
structure.generation_note: emit at least one IDAT between the head chunks and IEND; the payloads must concatenate into one zlib stream, so the simplest correct generator emits a single IDAT holding a complete stored-block zlib datastream

structure.subject: chunk type "IDAT"
structure.detail: multiple IDAT chunks must appear consecutively with no other chunk type between them
structure.description: The IDAT payloads are slices of one compressed stream, so interleaving any other chunk breaks the stream.
structure.generation_note: generate the IDAT run as one indivisible block, never as independently placed chunks in the shuffled middle section

structure.subject: chunk type "IHDR"
structure.detail: exactly 1
structure.description: Exactly one image header per datastream.
structure.generation_note: fixed head element, never part of the repeated section

structure.subject: chunk type "IEND"
structure.detail: exactly 1
structure.description: Exactly one image trailer per datastream.
structure.generation_note: fixed tail element, never part of the repeated section

structure.subject: chunk type "PLTE"
structure.detail: at most 1
structure.description: A datastream may contain no more than one palette.
structure.generation_note: emit as an optional single element in the pre-IDAT head, not in the repeated array

structure.subject: chunk type "PLTE"
structure.detail: must appear after IHDR and before the first IDAT
structure.description: The palette must be known before any image data is decoded.
structure.generation_note: place in the fixed pre-IDAT section

structure.subject: chunk type "PLTE"
structure.detail: mandatory when PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.color_type is 3
structure.condition: only when the colour type is 3 (Indexed)
structure.description: Indexed-colour images cannot be decoded without a palette.
structure.generation_note: make PLTE emission conditional on the colour type chosen for IHDR rather than random

structure.subject: chunk type "PLTE"
structure.detail: must not appear when PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.color_type is 0 or 4
structure.condition: only when the colour type is greyscale (0) or greyscale with alpha (4)
structure.description: A palette is meaningless for greyscale images and its presence is a spec violation.
structure.generation_note: suppress PLTE entirely for greyscale colour types

structure.subject: chunk types "cHRM", "gAMA", "iCCP", "sBIT", "sRGB"
structure.detail: must appear after IHDR, before PLTE (if present), and before the first IDAT
structure.description: Colour-space chunks affect how PLTE and IDAT are interpreted, so they must precede both.
structure.generation_bound: at most 1 of each; at most 5 chunks total from this group
structure.generation_note: emit as an optional, order-preserving block between IHDR and PLTE

structure.subject: chunk types "bKGD", "hIST", "tRNS"
structure.detail: must appear after PLTE (if PLTE is present) and before the first IDAT
structure.description: These chunks reference palette entries or sample values, so they follow the palette and precede the image data.
structure.generation_bound: at most 1 of each; at most 3 chunks total from this group
structure.generation_note: emit as an optional block between PLTE and the IDAT run

structure.subject: chunk types "pHYs", "sPLT"
structure.detail: must appear after IHDR and before the first IDAT; their position relative to PLTE is unconstrained
structure.description: Physical dimensions and suggested palettes must be known before the image data is processed.
structure.generation_bound: at most 1 pHYs; at most 4 sPLT chunks
structure.generation_note: emit in the pre-IDAT section; each sPLT needs a unique paletteName

structure.subject: chunk types "cHRM", "gAMA", "iCCP", "sBIT", "sRGB", "bKGD", "hIST", "tRNS", "pHYs", "tIME"
structure.detail: at most 1 of each per datastream
structure.description: Each of these ancillary chunks may appear only once; a second copy is a spec violation even though the template happily parses any number.
structure.generation_note: model each as an independent optional element, not as members of a repeated array

structure.subject: chunk type "sPLT"
structure.detail: any number, but every sPLT must carry a paletteName distinct from every other sPLT in the file
structure.description: Multiple suggested palettes are allowed provided their names are unique.
structure.generation_bound: 0 to 4 sPLT chunks, each with at most 64 entries
structure.generation_note: if more than one is emitted, derive the names from the array index so uniqueness is structural

structure.subject: chunk types "tEXt", "zTXt", "iTXt"
structure.detail: any number, anywhere after IHDR and before IEND, before or after IDAT
structure.description: Text chunks are the only chunks with no ordering restriction beyond the IHDR/IEND bracket.
structure.generation_bound: 0 to 4 text chunks in total, each with a payload of at most 96 bytes
structure.generation_note: these are the natural payload of the bounded repeated middle section; keep the total count small so text does not crowd out structural coverage

structure.subject: chunk type "tIME"
structure.detail: may appear anywhere after IHDR and before IEND
structure.description: The modification-time chunk has no ordering constraint relative to PLTE or IDAT.
structure.generation_note: safe to place in the repeated middle section

structure.subject: chunk types "sRGB" and "iCCP"
structure.detail: at most one of the two may appear in a datastream
structure.description: sRGB and iCCP are competing declarations of the colour space and must not both be present.
structure.generation_bound: at most 1 chunk drawn from the pair
structure.generation_note: model as a union or a single optional slot that picks one of the two types

structure.subject: chunk type "hIST"
structure.detail: requires a PLTE chunk earlier in the datastream, and must contain exactly one uint16 per palette entry
structure.description: The palette histogram is defined only in terms of an existing palette.
structure.generation_bound: 0 or 1, and only when PLTE was emitted
structure.generation_note: gate hIST emission on the PLTE branch and derive its length from the palette entry count

structure.subject: chunk type "acTL"
structure.detail: must appear after IHDR and before the first IDAT
structure.description: The animation control chunk declares the file to be an APNG and must be seen before the default image.
structure.generation_note: emit at most one acTL in the pre-IDAT section, and only when generating an animated file

structure.subject: chunk type "fcTL"
structure.detail: requires a preceding acTL; the number of fcTL chunks must equal PNG_CHUNK_ACTL.num_frames; sequence numbers across fcTL and fdAT must run 0,1,2,... with no gaps
structure.description: Frame control chunks form a numbered sequence that acTL's frame count must match exactly.
structure.generation_bound: 1 to 4 fcTL chunks, matching the generated num_frames
structure.generation_note: generate frames as a bounded array and set num_frames from the array length, never independently; carry a single shared counter to fill every sequence_number in both fcTL and fdAT

structure.subject: chunk type "fdAT"
structure.detail: must appear after the first IDAT and after the fcTL that describes its frame; the fdAT chunks of one frame must be contiguous
structure.description: Frame data follows the default image and belongs to the most recent frame control chunk.
structure.generation_bound: 1 to 2 fdAT chunks per frame, each payload capped at 4096 bytes
structure.generation_note: emit each animation frame as the fixed pair [one fcTL][one or two fdAT], appended after the IDAT run and before IEND

structure.subject: chunk type "fcTL" describing the default image
structure.detail: if an fcTL appears before the first IDAT it makes IDAT the first animation frame, and that fcTL must carry sequence_number 0, the full IHDR width and height, zero offsets and blend_op APNG_BLEND_OP_SOURCE
structure.condition: only when the default image is part of the animation
structure.description: APNG allows the default image to double as frame 0, but only under strict geometry constraints.
structure.generation_note: the simpler and safer generation strategy is to keep every fcTL after IDAT, so the default image is not an animation frame at all

structure.subject: PNG_CHUNK
structure.detail: the chunk stream repeats until end of file with no spec maximum; the template loops `while(!FEof())`
structure.description: The top-level parse is an unbounded loop over chunks, which is what a generator must bound explicitly.
structure.generation_bound: 8 to 24 chunks total per file, including the mandatory IHDR, the IDAT run and IEND. With every payload capped at 4096 bytes this holds generated files under roughly 100 KiB, which keeps throughput high; an unbounded loop over a uint32 length field is the single easiest way for this format to produce multi-gigabyte outputs.
structure.generation_note: replace the while(!FEof()) loop with: fixed IHDR head, optional pre-IDAT ancillary block, a bounded IDAT run, a bounded array of freely-placeable chunks, an optional APNG frame array, then the fixed IEND tail

structure.subject: any bytes after the IEND chunk
structure.detail: the datastream ends with IEND's CRC; trailing bytes are not part of the PNG
structure.description: The template keeps looping until FEof and so silently parses trailing garbage as further chunks, but a conforming file has none.
structure.generation_note: stop writing immediately after IEND's CRC

evidence.snippet: error_message( "*ERROR: Chunk IEND must be last chunk." );

structure.subject: PNG_CHUNK field order
structure.detail: within every chunk the order is fixed: uint32 length, char[4] type, `length` payload bytes, uint32 CRC
structure.description: The chunk envelope is invariant across every chunk type, and the CRC always sits last.
structure.generation_bound: exactly these four elements per chunk, in this order
structure.generation_note: generate the payload first, then back-patch length, then compute the CRC over type plus payload; length and CRC can never be chosen before the payload exists

evidence.snippet: uint32  length;                      // Number of data bytes (not including length,type, or crc)

template_deviations.subject: PNG_CHUNK_TIME.timeYear, PNG_CHUNK_FCTL.delay_num, PNG_CHUNK_FCTL.delay_den
template_deviations.issue: Declared as int16 (signed) where the PNG and APNG specifications define unsigned 2-byte integers.
template_deviations.impact: A generator that respects the declared signed type will never emit values above 32767, silently shrinking the legal range by half; a parser will display large legal values as negative.
template_deviations.action: Treat all three as uint16 for generation.

template_deviations.subject: PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.data and PNG_CHUNK_FDAT.frame_data
template_deviations.issue: Both array sizes reference `length`, which is not a member of the struct they appear in; it is the enclosing PNG_CHUNK.length captured by 010 Editor's lexical scoping.
template_deviations.impact: The rewrite step must wire the enclosing chunk's length into these structs explicitly (as PNG_CHUNK_PLTE, PNG_CHUNK_ITXT, PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT and PNG_CHUNK_SPLT already do via their chunkLen parameter), or the generated code will not compile or will read the wrong value.
template_deviations.action: Pass length as an explicit parameter, matching the chunkLen convention used by the other length-dependent structs.

template_deviations.subject: PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.data, PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtValChunkData, PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData, PNG_CHUNK_SPLT.spltData, PNG_CHUNK_FDAT.frame_data
template_deviations.issue: Every one of these array sizes is a subtraction that can go negative when the length field is smaller than the variable-length prefix it describes. Nothing clamps the result.
template_deviations.impact: On malformed input the template computes a negative array size. On generation the same arithmetic means the length field and the string fields must be chosen together, never independently.
template_deviations.action: Generate the variable-length prefixes first, then derive the chunk length as prefix size plus a bounded payload size, guaranteeing a non-negative remainder.

template_deviations.subject: PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA
template_deviations.issue: The struct is typedef'd but never instantiated; the dispatch chain has no iCCP branch, so iCCP chunks are consumed by the generic ubyte data[length] path. Its second field is also named `red`, which is meaningless for iCCP: at that offset the format has the compression method byte.
template_deviations.impact: Constraints recorded for this type describe dead code unless the rewrite step adds an iCCP branch.
template_deviations.action: Either add an iCCP branch (profile name, compression method 0, then a zlib-compressed ICC profile) or leave iCCP on the generic path; do not generate PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA as written, since it omits the compressed-profile field entirely.

template_deviations.subject: PNG_CHUNK.length
template_deviations.issue: The length field is read and used directly as an array size with no bound check of any kind, not even against the 2^31-1 spec ceiling or the remaining file size.
template_deviations.impact: This is the template's laxest point and, for generation, the single most important field to bound. An unconstrained uint32 here produces multi-gigabyte files.
template_deviations.action: Always derive length from the payload actually generated, and cap generated payloads as recorded in the generation_range.

template_deviations.subject: PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData
template_deviations.issue: chunkLen/3 truncates rather than rejecting a length that is not a multiple of 3, and no upper bound of 256 entries is enforced.
template_deviations.impact: The parser accepts palettes the spec forbids; a generator must not imitate it.
template_deviations.action: Generate an entry count in 1..256 and set the chunk length to exactly three times it.

template_deviations.subject: signature and ordering checks
template_deviations.issue: The signature check at lines 367-373 aborts, but the IHDR-first and IEND-last checks at lines 381-387 only emit a warning and only run when CHUNK_CNT > 1, so a single-chunk file is never checked at all.
template_deviations.impact: The template will happily parse files with no IHDR and no IEND, which no decoder accepts.
template_deviations.action: Treat IHDR-first and IEND-last as hard structural requirements during generation regardless of the template's leniency.

template_deviations.subject: PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.bits, PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.width, PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.height
template_deviations.issue: The bit depth is a bare ubyte with no enum and no check, and the dimensions are unchecked uint32 values that are allowed to be zero.
template_deviations.impact: Uniform random generation here yields an IHDR that every real decoder rejects on its first check, so no generated file would reach the IDAT decoder.
template_deviations.action: Constrain bits to the five legal depths narrowed by colour type, and both dimensions to a small non-zero range.
